properties.description:

Carlsbad Caverns National Park, or 21 miles northeast of Pine
Springs, moving east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Carlsbad Caverns National Park.
properties.instruction:

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Persons in campgrounds should consider seeking sturdy shelter until
this storm passes.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 25 at 7:57PM MDT until October 25 at 8:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
SVRABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Eastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
Central Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 830 PM MDT.

* At 757 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 20 miles east of
Tinnie, or 22 miles west of Roswell, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Eastern Lincoln and Central Chaves Counties.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can
hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
West Central Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 145 AM MDT.

* At 750 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hagerman.

line due west of Dexter, NM. This heavy runoff is expected to flood
arroyos that flow into the Rio Felix, and expected to reach Hagerman,
NM later tonight into Monday morning.

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

dangerous flows in arroyos and over low water crossings.

just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
early Thursday morning.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Coastal areas of Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara,
and San Luis Obispo Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be Monday
through Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated
Coastal Flood Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger
surf develops.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Hawaii in Hawaii, HI; Oahu in Honolulu, HI; Kauai, HI; Maui, HI
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 25 at 3:08PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
ESFHFO

A significant pattern change is expected late Monday night through at
least Thursday as deep tropical moisture is brought north. A
combination of surface lows and troughs will bring exceptionally
moist air over the state beginning late Monday night. Heavy rain and
isolated thunderstorms are possible throughout this period. Models
have not converged on details yet, so exact locations, timing, and
rainfall amounts are not certain. Please be prepared for periods of
heavy rain this coming week.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through the
Internet (weather.gov/hawaii), local media, social media, or NOAA
Weather Radio broadcasts.

An updated outlook will be issued MOnday by 6 AM HST or sooner if
necessary.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 6:43PM MDT until October 25 at 9:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding continues, especially along the Conejos River

* WHERE...Southeastern Conejos County...

* WHEN...Until 915 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will continue across low-lying and flood-prone
locations, especially along and near the Conejos River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 643 PM MDT, River gauge reports indicate elevated river levels
continue due to multiple days of heavy rainfall. The Conejos
River at Mogote has crested, although high flows and flooding
will persist, especially downstream from Mogote to the confluence
with the Rio Grande.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford and Conejos.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 25 at 8:13PM EDT until October 26 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous
rip currents and large breaking waves expected in the surf
zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT
Thursday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT
Monday through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some
roads and low lying property including parking lots, parks,
lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience
shallow flooding. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers
away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can
throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom causing
neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will continue to rise with a
King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-week. The
morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily tides.
King Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.
